source.inspection: Independent inventory reviewer visually read all 22 source page images, printed 69–90, before reading chapter-IV authored preparations. Number, subpart, theory and review-question counts were derived directly from the source.

theory.title: Теорема о соотношениях между сторонами и углами треугольника

caseRequirements.228: Four labelled cases, including the admissible nondegenerate domain for the parameter alpha in cases в and г.
caseRequirements.231: Both claims: acute base angles and obtuse exterior angles at the base.
caseRequirements.233: Three labelled values. Where possible distinguish whether the specified angle is the vertex angle or a base angle; do not discard a valid configuration.
caseRequirements.236: Prove the converse median-half-side property from prior facts; point 35 has not yet been introduced at this exercise.
caseRequirements.239: The given 115-degree exterior angle may be at the vertex opposite the base or at a base vertex; consider both admissible triangles.
caseRequirements.241: Both side orderings and the separate question whether angle A may be obtuse.
caseRequirements.244: Non-strict median/altitude inequality; include equality when the midpoint is the perpendicular foot.
caseRequirements.252: Figure 136: retain both claims, including that AO meets BC at its midpoint and is perpendicular to BC.
caseRequirements.253: Two nonexistence cases; equality of one side and the sum of the other two is degenerate, not a triangle.
caseRequirements.255: Three labelled side pairs; test both candidates for the repeated side by the strict triangle inequality.
caseRequirements.256: Broken-line length is not less than endpoint distance; distinguish equality from strict inequality.
caseRequirements.268: The original triangle is explicitly acute; do not add the extraneous obtuse configuration.
caseRequirements.271: The points lie on the sides of angle O; explain why the ray OC is the interior bisector.
caseRequirements.272: Both given triangles are explicitly acute; use that constraint when identifying corresponding right triangles.
caseRequirements.274: The source states equality of two corresponding angles and BH=B1H1; allow feet on side extensions where appropriate.
caseRequirements.275: Construct a line through the interior point cutting equal segments on the angle sides; justify the construction.
caseRequirements.277: The third vertex is distinct from the diameter endpoints; the radius/median argument may be used without the later inscribed-angle theorem.
caseRequirements.278: Use the 15-degree acute angle, the median and altitude from the right vertex; CH=4 and the target is the whole hypotenuse AB.
caseRequirements.283: The point is on the base and equidistant from the two supporting lines of the lateral sides; prove the perpendicular conclusion.
caseRequirements.284: Include the line coinciding with the segment line: both distances are zero; avoid a nondegenerate triangle argument in that case.
caseRequirements.285: Lines b and c may be on the same or opposite sides of a, producing two distances.
caseRequirements.288: Locus lies strictly inside the nonstraight angle and at positive distance PQ from line BC; boundary intersection is excluded.
caseRequirements.289: For two distinct parallel lines the locus is their middle parallel line, with both inclusions justified.
caseRequirements.291: At a positive prescribed distance, both parallel lines are needed; if zero is discussed, the original line is the locus.
caseRequirements.292: Compass-and-straightedge construction has two parallel-line solutions, one on each side of a.
caseRequirements.293: Intersect the given line a with both distance-PQ parallels to b, obtaining the two possible points.
caseRequirements.294: Construct by a side, an adjacent angle and the bisector from that angle; include the existence restriction rather than assuming every positive bisector length works.
caseRequirements.295: Construct by the side, a median to one of the other sides and the included angle; identify the intended median correctly.
caseRequirements.296: Both angle-half and angle-quarter cases, with the sum of the two specified angles strictly below 180 degrees.
caseRequirements.297: One angle is the whole first given angle and the other is half the second; check the angle-sum existence condition.
caseRequirements.298: Two separate right-triangle constructions: both legs, and a leg plus its adjacent acute angle.
caseRequirements.299: All five constructions а–д, including base plus median to the base; include feasibility for base plus lateral side.
caseRequirements.300: Both transformed side triples; answer the explicit existence question using strict triangle inequalities.
caseRequirements.301: Preserve the source construction by a side, its adjacent angle and altitude to that side; obtuse adjacent angle gives an exterior foot.
caseRequirements.302: Two sides and the altitude to one of them may yield no, one or two noncongruent triangles; treat circle/parallel intersections and exclude degeneracy.
caseRequirements.303: Two sides and the median to one of them require a construction and existence analysis; midpoint versus side-endpoint coincidences are not triangles.
caseRequirements.307: Figure 152 has the full chain AP=PQ=QR=RB=BC and AB=AC; retain the point order P,R on AC and Q on AB.
caseRequirements.308: Prove both the interior foot from the obtuse vertex and the exterior feet from the acute vertices.
caseRequirements.309: Both equal and ordered projections; do not use the later Pythagorean theorem without proof.
caseRequirements.310: Both converse claims, with equal or ordered obliques; do not use the later Pythagorean theorem without proof.
caseRequirements.311: Strict median inequality; use a reflected vertex and the triangle inequality.
caseRequirements.312: M is strictly inside the triangle and the inequality is strict.
caseRequirements.314: The source explicitly requests proof by contradiction.
caseRequirements.318: AB>AC is given; correctly order angles B and C and consider altitude feet on extensions.
caseRequirements.321: The strict inequality requires the point on the open opposite side; if endpoints are discussed, state the necessary boundary qualification.
caseRequirements.322: Two sides and the median to the third side; construct using an auxiliary triangle with twice the median and state strict triangle inequalities.
caseRequirements.323: All three right-triangle constructions: hypotenuse/acute angle, leg/opposite angle, hypotenuse/leg.
caseRequirements.324: Nine labelled compass-and-straightedge angles: а30, б60, в15, г120, д150, е135, ж165, з75, и105 degrees; not protractor measurements.
caseRequirements.325: Side, altitude to it and median to one of the other sides: handle intersection counts and degenerate cases.
caseRequirements.326: D on AB, E on BC, DE parallel AC and DE=AD+CE; preserve all constraints in construction and proof.
caseRequirements.327: Given equilateral ABC and B1 on AC; construct A1 on BC and C1 on AB with A1B1C1 equilateral. Treat endpoint cases explicitly if admitting them.
caseRequirements.328: Given angle, altitude and bisector are all from the same vertex; analyze zero/one/two solutions and degenerate angle cases.
caseRequirements.329: Given side with altitude and median both to it; compare median and height, and exclude the collinear case.
caseRequirements.330: ABC is right at A; M lies on AB and its distance to line BC must equal AM, not a different prescribed segment.
